name: Month/quarter-end pension rebalancing flow (Calendar rebalancing signal), equity-bond and month-end FX fix leg
author_year: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone, 2025 (NBER WP 33554, revised Jan 2026; not peer-reviewed)
instrument: Paper: S&P 500 futures vs 10-year Treasury note futures. Maven MT5 mapping: US500/US100 index CFD vs a US 10Y bond CFD [uncertain: 10Y bond CFD availability on Maven not verified]. FX leg: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY [uncertain: FX leg not tested in the paper; it is a separate industry-claimed flow].
timeframe: Daily close-to-close signal (paper). Execution window: last 4-5 trading days of the month. Intraday only as a sensitivity check (paper footnote: using 3:30 PM prices gives largely the same results).
entry_rule: Calendar signal = equity weight deviation from a 60/40 target, measured at the prior close from daily equity and bond returns. Paper's sign: when equities are overweight they tend to underperform bonds over the following days, so the trade is short equity / long bond when equity is overweight, and the reverse when underweight. Entry window: last 4-5 trading days of the month (paper finds predictability peaks in the last four days and that pensions avoid trading on the very last day). Exact entry day and time inside that window: [uncertain].
exit_rule: Hold through the month-end window, exit at a close inside the window. Paper does not give a fixed exit rule for a retail implementation; its cost calculation assumes trades concentrated in the last week of the month. Exact exit day: [uncertain].
stop_rule: No stop defined in the paper. A stop is not part of the tested rule. If one is added, any level would be a discretionary choice [uncertain].
holding_time: About 4-5 trading days per month-end window (multi-day, daily resolution).
trades_per_year: About 12 windows per year for the Calendar rule (one per month). The paper's cost estimate uses 12 trades per year for the Calendar strategy. Quarter-end windows are a subset of these 12.
overnight_weekend: Yes. A multi-day hold crosses overnight sessions and weekends.
signal_window_definition: Paper uses a dummy for the last N days of the month, with N=4 peaking in t-statistics; the main specification uses the last week (Dummy 5 days). Returns are daily close-to-close, S&P 500 futures minus 10Y note futures. Intraday: the paper checks 3:30 PM prices as a sensitivity and reports largely the same results. DST: not discussed in the paper, which works at daily frequency [uncertain for any intraday Maven version].
sample_period: Main daily regressions: 1997-09-10 to 2023-03-17. Predictability became significant in the early 2000s (paper). Longer daily test (Kenneth French data) from 1961 to 2023 is reported in Table 4 for the Threshold signal only [uncertain for the Calendar signal in that table]. No 2023-2026 sample.
out_of_sample: No formal out-of-sample trading test was found in the sections read. The paper uses in-sample predictive regressions with HAC/heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. The front-running strategy is a real-time construction, but on the in-sample period. No post-2023 result. [uncertain: not verified in the full appendix].
cost_assumption: Paper's rebalancer cost estimate: Calendar implied cost about 5 bps per year (|-0.39| x 1% x 12 trades); Threshold about 11 bps under a conservative assumption; total about 8 bps per year for institutions. Paper does not model retail CFD spreads or swap. Maven measured cost: [uncertain: not measured yet; the project rule requires a Maven reality_profiler measurement before pre-registration].
reported_metrics: Front-running strategy (S&P 500 futures vs 10Y futures, Table 6 Panel A): annual excess return 10.20%, volatility 9.17%, Sharpe 1.11, skewness 5.23. Same-sample comparison: S&P 500 Sharpe 0.35, 10Y Sharpe 0.48. Alphas in Table 6 Panel B: not extracted [uncertain]. Costs are not deducted in the summary table as read [uncertain].
third_party_replication: No independent academic replication found. Industry commentary (Full FX, Concretum, Goldman Sachs desk notes) describes flows, not a tested out-of-sample rule. Paper cites a 16-pension roundtable that confirmed mechanical rebalancing, which is not a replication of returns [uncertain: independent quant replication not found].
evidence_grade: Working paper (NBER, explicitly not peer-reviewed). Supplementary: industry blogs (not evidence grade).
decay_status: Paper reports predictive power became significant in the early 2000s, linked to pension allocation changes and 2006 target-date fund legislation, which implies the effect is not constant over time. No formal decay test found. Not tested after March 2023 [uncertain].
regime_split: Yes, partly: significant from the early 2000s (paper); the 1997-2023 Threshold coefficient in Table 4 is -0.3685 versus -0.1809 for 1961-2023, so the post-1997 sample shows stronger predictability. Calendar-specific split not extracted [uncertain]. Front-running strategy performs better in high-friction periods (paper Panel C).
data_source_requirement: Daily closes for an equity index and a long-duration bond. Maven MT5 daily or M15 bars are enough for a close-to-close version. Bond leg needs a 10Y CFD or proxy [uncertain: availability on Maven]. No options, tick, or flow data needed for the signal, but the paper's flow confirmation uses CFTC COT and ICI data, which are not on Maven.
min_lot_fit_5k10k: 0.01 US100 = $0.10 per point. A stop-free multi-day hold has no defined risk. If a hypothetical 200-point stop is applied: $20 risk on 0.01 lot = 0.4% of a 5K account and 0.2% of a 10K account [uncertain: index level and stop are assumptions].
fn_rule_fit: Open risk within FN 3% at 0.01 lot. Weekend hold is allowed. No HFT, grid, or tick-scalp pattern. High-impact news rule: the month-end window often overlaps the US payrolls / ISM release on the first business day of the month and quarter-end data; the +-5 minute rule is not checked against a release calendar [uncertain].
bot_policy_compliance: Yes in principle: rule-based daily signal, one position, no messaging link needed.
event_overlap: Last business day 16:00 London WM/Reuters fix; US closing auction (MOC); quarter-end coincides with the March/June/September/December third-Friday expiration (triple witching) and S&P quarterly rebalance; first-business-day US data releases at the start of the next month.
overlap_with_existing: Low expected overlap with SWEEP_CORE (intraday US100 sweep), Donchian XAU, Noise Band, and BTC 21-23 UTC because this is a multi-day calendar rule. Exact overlap not measured [uncertain].
rejected_catalog_hit: Two related vetoes. (1) turn_of_month_plus1 (REJECTED): S&P 500 +7.6 bp vs +5.0 bp on other days (2012-2026, n=178), NQ +14.0 vs +7.0 bp, Bonferroni CIs include zero, 2022+ S&P +3.8 bp. Same calendar family, different window. (2) fx_fix_reversal_london_tokyo (REJECTED): London 16:00 fix reversal has no gross effect; for the FX leg this is a direct veto. Command 'elenenler --kontrol rebalans' returned no entry.
base_rate_check: Yes, the month-end effect is a known calendar pattern, so the test must compare against the turn-of-month base rate and matched non-month-end days. The paper's signal is conditioned on portfolio deviation, which is not a pure base rate, but the turn-of-month catalog veto shows the calendar part alone is weak after controls [uncertain for the paper's signal].
pitfall_risk: Post-hoc window choice (N=4 days picked from in-sample t-stat plots). Base-rate overlap with turn-of-month (vetoed in catalog). Overlapping multi-day windows make the 12 yearly observations non-independent. Small effective sample: about 25 years x 12 windows = about 300 windows. Costs not measured on Maven. Sign flips with signal definition (equity overweight vs underweight).
